caption:
Your heartbeat starts in the heart itself. A tiny cluster of cells called the sinoatrial node fires an electrical signal about 60 to 100 times a minute at rest, and your brain only nudges the speed.

That is why donor hearts can keep beating in a machine on the way to surgery. Transplanted hearts, cut off from their nerves, often rest faster, at around 90 to 110 bpm. Save this for the next time someone says the brain runs everything. Follow for a new body fact you didn't know, every day.

Would you rather have a heart run by your brain, or one that runs itself?
